title: I support everyone making their own games as first game developer using AI tools
author: Novel-Common9013
selftext: You guys doing really good job! Do not listen who says "AI Slop" to your game!

comments.author: scroteymcb
comments.body: I guess it's a subjective argument but you do see a fair few gams that have maybe had a week spent on them and are technically "AI Slop". In saying that some genius things can be made in a short period of time.

replies.author: TMiyoshi
replies.body: Yeah, a lot of "AI slop" I wouldn't play if human hands made it either. It's just people vibe coding a prototype in a few days and acting like they've made a complete game that rivals best of the best.

replies.author: Dazzling-Extent-5137
replies.body:
I think I spent a couple of months on my game, 4-5 hours per week, time allowing. But I specifically kept double checking, reviewing, rethinking a lot of things. AI was great help but without supervision it would have been a mess, full of inconsistencies.

With the experience I have now, it would have been half of that, but I still don't think you can do more than a "decent demo" within a week, unless you're cloning something and AI already knows exactly what to do.

And what I specifically learned - AI can't cover real human testing. It will find some mechanical issues but it will ignore a lot of stuff a real human will be bothered by.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: Im with you. Make whatever you wanna make. Make ai slop, who cares. A lot of games back then and now were just things cobbled together at times. Dont let others dictate your vision.

comments.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
comments.body: For real don’t let someone who’s chronically online and doesn’t produce anything ruin your mood. Some people get dopamine from setting goals and finishing them, some people get it through being insufferable on Reddit.

replies.author: Novel-Common9013
replies.body:
I heard "AI Slop" term at least 1000 times during development progress. 

I carried this heavy burden alone, but remember, "AI" is just a tool.   
  
The real talent lies in the creativity within you.

comments.author: PerfectSituation1668
comments.body:
Most people are worried that it is a new version of an assetflip, and that in itself was the new version of shovelware. I've seen some games now that where not so original and did not have consistent art because of AI, but the gameloop itself was good. It feels like those old flash games where people just experimented with stuff.

Pro tip: Do not prompt too generic, get creative with the prompts as well. I've seen the same goblins now over and over. Probably ChatGPTs fault with their goblin fetish. Go furter than just prompting "knight, wizard, goblin" because that's how you get standard stuff. Also if you make it pixelart, make it so that you use the same resolutions on your art. Think outside the box.

But if it's your first game and you're learning stuff (and you're having fun without costing you too much), then let nothing stop you. Even the people who like to do everything without AI get the "AI Slop" comments sometimes. Personally I don't use AI in my hobby projects, but that's because I want to, not because some trolls on the internet told me to. So you do you and have fun building stuff!

replies.author: PerfectSituation1668
replies.body: This is true. I always find it positive if someone makes a good game and forgive the mistakes if it's good. It was just my neutral observations about it. My stuff is also slop and I don't use AI. Maybe if I made something with AI in the future it won't be slop. It's just a tool in my opinion, but I am still in the I-want-to-do-everything-by-hand-type. So yeah, you are correct. It's not the tool, it's the person(s) making it.

comments.author: Chacudno

Releasing my first mobile game around the first, AI coded i did everything else.

Learned how to integrate claude code and now my second game is coming along 10x faster and looks so much better already. 

I love AI! The coding alone would have taken me months upon months to learn.

comments.author: davesoft
comments.body:
And as someone who's been coding my whole life, I'm eager to see people's ideas liberated from the difficulty of implementation. I've spent months on projects in the past only to conclude 'works, but isnt fun', now I can do that in half a day, maybe an hour if the idea is simple enough.

Don't make tools. Tell me a story. An old man has lost his fishing rod, what crazy adventures could you get up to finding the fishing rod?

comments.author: Embarrassed_Depth646
comments.body:
If you can design and build a good game, how you got there isn't important...do people like it?  Is it fun?  Is it a good game?  The obsession with AI and hating all things AI is no different than hating power tools or assembly lines or computers in general.  Why not use the tools available?

IMO, it's the end product that matters.  Human made garbage is still garbage.  AI made garbage is still garbage.  Working with AI, you're the lead developer and you are still responsible for putting out a good product.  If you fail, it's AI slop, but if you had humans working under you, it would still be the same slop...it would just take a lot more time and money to get to the same point.  Using AI does not make it bad or good...the developer and the design do.

I can understand people hating AAA companies for using AI rather than hiring humans, but it's just petty to be contemptuous of solo or small group developers.  Not everyone can hire a team or quit their job to become full time developers.
